Each sample opens a new session (m1_qualify._assembly_during_build), so that turn had no catalogue, and its retrieval read every page of the current epoch's catalogue inline (memory_session._catalogue_for; one route call per 256 files): 9 pages, 20 calls, 6694.4 ms at build progress 0.216, 17 pages, 28 calls, 10497.2 ms at build progress 0.413, 28 pages, 39 calls, 14762.7 ms at build progress 0.678, 35 pages, 46 calls, 23322.7 ms at build progress 0.857. The other 15 during-build turns took 11 calls or fewer and at most 2,520 ms. The product pays the same: its runner assembles the pack first (agent/runner.py:1815, _turn_context, memory.assemble at :1921) and only then calls repo_map (:1824), so a person's first turn in a session during a build reads the whole catalogue inside assembly. A long-lived session re-reads it inside a turn whenever its catalogue is older than CATALOGUE_SECONDS (60 s) and the build has published since. Measured as the limit is written; a disposition is owed.
